candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational bloodborne-pathogen exposure prevention
candidate.client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that OSHA requires a written Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan for employers with occupationally exposed employees, including exposure determination and implementation of required protective measures.

options.A: A written plan that includes an exposure determination and how required exposure-control measures will be implemented
options.B: A plan limited to employees who work in operating rooms
options.C: A plan based only on whether employees routinely wear personal protective equipment
options.D: A financial-loss plan that does not address occupational exposure incidents

candidate.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c) requires an employer with employees who have occupational exposure to establish a written Exposure Control Plan designed to eliminate or minimize employee exposure. Required elements include an exposure determination and the schedule and method for implementing specified protective provisions, including methods of compliance and post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. The exposure determination is made without regard to personal protective equipment. Therefore A is correct; B, C, and D conflict with the regulation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Employers with occupationally exposed employees must establish a written Exposure Control Plan that includes exposure determination and implementation of required protective provisions; exposure determination is made without regard to PPE.
candidate.source_locator: 1910.1030(c)(1)(i)-(ii), Exposure Control Plan; 1910.1030(c)(2)(i)-(ii), Exposure determination; related implementation provisions in 1910.1030(d)-(h)
candidate.stem: An employer has employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials. Which requirement belongs in the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Control Plan?
